schema: CREATE TABLE departments (dept_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, dept_name TEXT NOT NULL, location TEXT, manager_name TEXT);CREATE TABLE employees (emp_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, emp_name TEXT, dept_id INTEGER, role TEXT, FOREIGN KEY (dept_id) REFERENCES departments(dept_id));
correct_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T2.role) FROM departments AS T1 INNER JOIN employees AS T2 ON T1.dept_id = T2.dept_id WHERE T1.location = 'NYC'

expected_semantic_errors_to_be_caught.description: Used COUNT(DISTINCT primary_key) instead of COUNT(DISTINCT non_key_column). Since PK is always unique, this counts all matching rows rather than distinct role values.
